text:
codehygiene

An offline linter that flags hard-to-read code by its shape.

Source is read as a grid of bytes, not words, so names and spelling are ignored. The model is an 8 KB file of ternary weights that are programmed in compile.py , not trained. It runs on NumPy and covers 20+ languages.

 Install

 

 Use

 

Clean files print nothing. A flagged file prints its score, the flagged lines, and a target shape that scores cleaner:

 

Each ■ is two bytes of code, and <-N marks the source line a row came from.

 What gets flagged

 Kind Looks like 
 :--- :--- 
 deep nesting 4+ levels of indentation inside a function 
 dense line long call chains, nested ternaries, several statements on one line 
 cramped layout 20+ lines with no blank line, or ragged indentation 
 duplicate block the same 4+ lines pasted nearby, even with renamed variables 
 repetitive structure 4+ if x == ... branches in a row 
 comment echo comments that restate the next line, or commented-out code 

Bugs, type errors, and security issues are out of scope. Newly written or changed code is the intended target, not whole legacy repositories.

 Benchmarks

 v0.7.0 
 :--- :--- 
 Size 8 KB of weights, NumPy only 
 Speed (warm CPU) about 5 ms for 12 lines, 15 ms for 65, 70 ms for 333 
 Browser same scores as Python 

 Python and JavaScript

 

The same model runs in browsers and Node through codehygiene/engine.js .

install.title: Install
install.html:
# As an agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, ...)
npx skills add brianbell-x/codehygiene -g

# Or run once without installing
uvx --from git+https://github.com/brianbell-x/codehygiene codehygiene path/to/file.py --check
